section_summary: This section moves from the final tables of a Japanese labor union survey to U.S. occupation records on union rights, government employee legislation, and labor disputes. It includes diplomatic correspondence, legal analyses, translated Japanese notices, membership statistics, press material, and proposals for strengthening democratic trade unions.

subfiles.title: Labor Union Survey Report: concluding tables, errata, and colophon
subfiles.from: Japanese Ministry of Labor, Labor Statistics and Research Bureau
subfiles.about: Concluding tables classify Japanese unions by affiliation, staff, and associated activities.
subfiles.summary: The tables report full-time union staff and associated activities by region and federation. An errata page and publication details close the report, issued on May 30, 1948.

subfiles.title: Principles for Japanese Trade Unions: instructions to U.S. FEC member
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Authorizes answers to questions about FEC labor policy and MacArthur's July 22 letter.
subfiles.summary: Provides an attached statement and authorized responses concerning labor law, the July 31 ordinance, and pending revisions.

subfiles.title: Statement regarding implementation of FEC O45/5
subfiles.about: Explains Japan's Labor Relations Adjustment Law and labor dispute settlement record.
subfiles.summary: Describes conciliation, mediation, arbitration, strike limits, and labor committee procedures. Cites statistics through April 1948 to argue that the committees settled most disputes involving third-party intervention.

subfiles.title: Revision of ordinance on officials of wartime labor organizations
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports an exemption procedure allowing some former wartime labor officials to hold union office.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 671 explains the September revision and its criteria, arguing that individual review is more democratic than a blanket purge.

subfiles.title: Japanese notice and ordinance amendment concerning labor purge exemptions
subfiles.about: Sets out the amendment and application procedure for exemptions from restrictions on former wartime labor officials.
subfiles.summary: The enclosed Japanese text contains the September 13 ordinance amendment and September 16 ministerial notice. Its OCR is fragmented, but the following English translation gives the operative provisions.

subfiles.title: Translation of Labor Ministry notice No. 15 and ordinance amendment
subfiles.about: Explains narrow exemptions for former wartime labor officials and the required applications.
subfiles.summary: Governors must investigate applicants' wartime activity, opposition to militarism, and likely contribution to democratic unions. The annexed September 13 amendment authorizes the competent minister to grant exceptional exemptions.

subfiles.title: Changes in final text of Japan's National Public Service Law
subfiles.about: Analyzes late changes to government employees' organization rights and criminal penalties.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum argues that the introduced bill weakens employees' freedom to choose organizations and representatives while barring collective agreements. It highlights new penalties for organizing prohibited groups or instigating dispute tactics. The writer says these provisions diverge from earlier understandings with SCAP and could provoke strong U.S. labor opposition.

subfiles.title: National Public Service Law, Article 98
subfiles.about: Reproduces provisions on government employees' organizations, negotiations, strikes, and employment rights.
subfiles.summary: Article 98 permits employee organizations and limited negotiation while excluding specified services, prohibiting strikes and slowdown tactics, and prescribing loss of employment rights.

subfiles.title: National Public Service Law, Article 101 and supplementary provisions
subfiles.about: Reproduces limits on paid-time union work and registration rules for existing employee associations.
subfiles.summary: Existing government worker unions may continue under democratic procedures but must register with the National Personnel Authority.

subfiles.title: Japanese participation in World Federation of Trade Unions congress
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Advises against authorizing a Japanese delegation while deferring a definitive answer.
subfiles.summary: Concurs with Hepler's view and notes that a WFTU congress may not occur amid organizational division.

subfiles.title: Proposed Japanese participation in World Federation of Trade Unions congress
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese union plans to send delegates to a proposed WFTU congress.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 751 recounts Hepler's meeting with Watanabe Michio's delegation. Hepler opposes attendance but prefers a technical reason for refusal to limit communist propaganda.

subfiles.title: Japan delegates to WFTU to be elected by laborers
subfiles.about: Describes union preparations and election plans for a Japanese WFTU delegation.
subfiles.summary: Representatives of about forty unions discuss direct election of delegates, a January deadline, and their approach to GHQ Labor Chief Hepler.

subfiles.title: Cover memorandum on National Public Service Law changes
subfiles.about: Forwards an appraisal of restrictive changes in Japan's enacted public service law.
subfiles.summary: Warns that late changes curtailed government workers' rights more severely than anticipated and may require Departmental review.

subfiles.title: Soviet press commentary on Japanese trade unions
subfiles.about: Transmits a summary or translation of Soviet press claims about Japan's union movement.
subfiles.summary: The heavily damaged OCR describes strikes, communist influence, disputes with reformist union leaders, and struggles over Japanese trade union organization.

subfiles.title: Response proposed to MacArthur telegram C 66781
subfiles.about: Proposes investigating an anonymous labor policy statement and issuing a joint State-Army correction.
subfiles.summary: Recommends identifying the press source, publishing a corrective statement, and informing MacArthur.

subfiles.title: Draft radio to General MacArthur
subfiles.about: Drafts a State-Army statement on labor's responsibilities under Japan's recovery program.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes dissemination of the statement and promises investigation of the anonymous press source.

subfiles.title: MacArthur telegram C 66781 on Associated Press strike story
subfiles.to: Department of the Army, Under Secretary Draper
subfiles.about: Objects to a Washington press report asserting that Japanese unions retain strike rights.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur argues that the report undermines the occupation's economic recovery program and encourages disruptive groups. He urges action against anonymous official statements that appear to conflict with SCAP policy.

subfiles.title: Morris Harris story: return of attachments
subfiles.about: Returns papers concerning the Morris Harris story and notes Draper's pending reply.
subfiles.summary: Returns attachments and asks that Eichler's note be passed to Colonel Skidmore for Major Miller.

subfiles.title: Japanese government workers labor legislation: summary
subfiles.about: Reviews the 1948 dispute over Japanese government workers' strike, bargaining, and organization rights.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum traces MacArthur's July 1948 letter, Japan's interim ordinance, U.S. interdepartmental objections, SCAP replies, and Far Eastern Commission debate. It records disagreement over whether FEC labor principles cover government workers and whether communications employees should receive collective bargaining rights. It also considers diplomatic efforts to avert further FEC action.

subfiles.title: Japanese labor union membership
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese Ministry of Labor membership and local union statistics.
subfiles.summary: Reports 6,852,287 union members and 36,132 local unions as of December 31, 1948.

subfiles.title: Labor union membership in major federations
subfiles.about: Lists membership and local unions affiliated with major national labor organizations.
subfiles.summary: Compares federation memberships and notes the national total of 6,852,287 union members.

subfiles.title: Government workers' unions
subfiles.about: Lists Japanese government worker unions with union and membership counts.
subfiles.summary: Covers railway, communications, tax, local government, finance, and teachers' unions.

subfiles.title: Incoming telegram concerning Japanese administrative system
subfiles.about: A badly damaged telegram refers to a statement concerning Japan's administrative system.
subfiles.summary: Most substantive text is illegible in the supplied OCR.

subfiles.title: Removal of union officials from company payrolls
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports GHQ's order to end employer payment of full-time union officials.
subfiles.summary: Explains that employer-financed union officers violate the Trade Union Law and undermine union independence.

subfiles.title: Union officials ordered removed from company payrolls
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Far East Command, Public Information Office
subfiles.about: Announces enforcement of the Trade Union Law's ban on employer financing of unions.
subfiles.summary: Hepler says unions must remove full-time officials from company payrolls within ninety days of an announced effective date. He argues that employer funding compromises democratic union leadership.

subfiles.title: Gibson letter forwarding report on Japanese labor
subfiles.about: Forwards recommendations from Gibson's recent visit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Urges measures to strengthen democratic trade unions and counter communist influence.

subfiles.title: Report of John W. Gibson, Assistant Secretary of Labor
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Army; Department of State
subfiles.about: Recommends labor law reforms and measures to strengthen democratic Japanese unions.
subfiles.summary: Gibson urges public service law revision, bargaining rights for communications workers, flexible wage controls, a shorter government workweek, and a minimum wage. He proposes U.S. labor exchanges and assistance to democratic anti-communist union leaders.

subfiles.title: Reply to Gibson on Japanese labor recommendations
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Gibson's report and proposes further discussion of its recommendations.
subfiles.summary: Notes renewed U.S. efforts to secure collective bargaining for Japanese communications workers and says Gibson's proposals are under study.

subfiles.title: Sending a committee of U.S. labor leaders to Japan
subfiles.about: Recommends a labor adviser to MacArthur in place of a visiting U.S. labor mission.
subfiles.summary: Bishop weighs criticism of SCAP labor policy, an Australian FEC proposal, and possible public service law revisions. He recommends appointing a trusted labor adviser who could improve union practices and help address the policy dispute.

subfiles.title: Despatch concerning a Shibaura labor petition
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Discusses contacts over a Shibaura-related petition and possible Allied Council consideration.
subfiles.summary: The supplied page begins a despatch on a petition involving Shibaura and Allied Council member Shaw; its OCR is substantially damaged.
